entities.name: Álmos, Duke of Nitra
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Álmos, Duke of Nitra, was a pivotal figure in 12th-century Hungarian dynastic politics, known for his relentless and ultimately unsuccessful struggle for the Hungarian throne against his brother, King Coloman. His ambition, fueled by a claim to primogeniture (though not strictly established in Hungary at the time), led to decades of internal conflict and foreign interventions, profoundly shaping the Arpád dynasty's succession practices and Hungary's early medieval geopolitical landscape. Born to King Géza I, his life was defined by a tragic rivalry that saw him repeatedly challenge royal authority from his power base as Duke of Nitra and later as a pretender seeking external support.

Álmos's early career saw him govern the Duchy of Nitra, a significant semi-autonomous territory within the Kingdom of Hungary, from around 1095. Upon the death of his father, Géza I, the throne passed to his uncle Ladislaus I, and then to his younger brother Coloman in 1095. Despite an initial agreement where Álmos would retain his ducal lands, their relationship quickly deteriorated into open conflict. Álmos repeatedly sought refuge and military aid from neighboring powers, including the Holy Roman Empire (under Henry V) and Poland (under Bolesław III Wrymouth), attempting to depose Coloman. These attempts led to several campaigns, truces, and renewed hostilities, culminating in his blinding along with his young son Béla (the Blind) by Coloman's order in 1113, a brutal act intended to eliminate any future claim to the throne.
